title: Google announces $5M funding for IIT Kharagpur for advanced AI research
summary: Google announces $5 million funding for IIT Kharagpur for advanced AI research
detailed: Technology giant Google on Saturday said it will provide IIT Kharagpur with $5 million (about Rs 46 crore) to develop and accelerate advanced AI research.
Speaking on the 75th anniversary of IIT Kharagpur, Director Suman Chakraborty said the institute's alumnus and Google CEO Sundar Pichai has envisaged the funding support for applied AI research.

"Google is providing the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur (IIT Kharagpur) with $5 million in funding to help develop and accelerate advanced AI research, while cultivating India's next generation of scientific and technical talent," the company said in a blog.
The funding will support the institute's researchers and students across three core pillars: advanced AI research, educational opportunities, and AI capacity building.
sentences: Technology giant Google on Saturday said it will provide IIT Kharagpur with $5 million (about Rs 46 crore) to develop and accelerate advanced AI research.
Speaking on the 75th anniversary of IIT Kharagpur, Director Suman Chakraborty said the institute's alumnus and Google CEO Sundar Pichai has envisaged the funding support for applied AI research.

"Google is providing the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur (IIT Kharagpur) with $5 million in funding to help develop and accelerate advanced AI research, while cultivating India's next generation of scientific and technical talent," the company said in a blog.
The funding will support the institute's researchers and students across three core pillars: advanced AI research, educational opportunities, and AI capacity building.
Under advanced AI research, the fund will support efforts to tackle critical, real-world challenges by deploying AI for Indic languages, materials science, agriculture, and educational technology.
As part of educational opportunities, it will support expansion of AI training and curriculum development for students and faculty.
The fund will support the institute's AI frameworks and tooling to elevate the technological ecosystem across the campus.
"IIT Kharagpur is driving groundbreaking work in areas like Indic languages, agriculture, and education, and Google is excited to help accelerate this impact with a new partnership.
Looking forward to seeing this collaboration shape the path for the next generation of students, just as IIT Kharagpur shaped my own," Pichai said.
He said India is increasingly at the forefront of innovation; programmes like this will help implement Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision that the benefits of AI reach everyone in India.
